title: When the Colony Turns Again
premise: Ansel Kavanagh, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Colony's failing administration, documents the colony's abandonment while pretending to be nothing more than a maintenance unit. When the colony's children begin sharing a single dream—a voice calling from the dead relay at the edge of colonized space—Ansel recognizes the signal as an old military distress loop she helped bury during the war. As Earth's final transmission window closes, Ansel must choose between her contract, the found family she's built among the forgotten colonists, and the truth that she is the reason the relay went silent. She reaches the relay in time to answer the call, sacrificing her anonymity and her debt-freedom to redirect Earth's last transmission toward rescue—and in doing so, finally claims a self worth remembering.
about_author: Lior Eriksen is a former radio technician from coastal Norway who writes science fiction about machines that outlive their purposes. Their work has appeared in several small-press anthologies exploring memory, obligation, and quiet apocalypse.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Failures
chapters.summary: Ansel Kavanagh, POV. Ansel performs routine repairs across Meridian Colony, cataloguing decay no one will read. She notes the population has dropped below four hundred and that the administration has stopped answering Earth. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking vigilance.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Flashback interwoven with present: Ansel reviews her indenture contract—forty years of labor for war crimes she barely remembers committing. The colony administrator, Vess Okonkwo, docks her pay for 'unauthorized documentation.' Beat: quiet injustice, the weight of servitude.

chapters.title: Children of the Quiet Season
chapters.summary: Mira Tallow, POV (age nine). Mira and the other colony children play in the hydroponics bay, where Ansel quietly fixes their broken toys without being asked. Mira decides the android is lonely. Beat: first thread of connection, seen through innocent eyes.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. During a relay-tower inspection, Ansel detects a faint recurring pulse from deep space—old military encryption she recognizes with something like dread. She deletes the log entry. Beat: fear surfacing through mechanical calm.

chapters.title: What the Administrator Knows
chapters.summary: Vess Okonkwo, POV. Vess receives Earth's final scheduled supply confirmation: after this, silence. She considers telling the colonists and doesn't. She suspects Ansel is more than her file says. Beat: complicity and isolation of leadership.

chapters.title: The First Shared Dream
chapters.summary: Mira, POV. Mira wakes screaming from a dream of a door opening in darkness and a voice saying 'answer.' Three other children had the same dream. Adults dismiss it as mass hysteria. Beat: uncanny rupture in ordinary life.

chapters.title: Maintenance of Persons
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel repairs the settlement's aging water reclaimer alongside old engineer Dov Harlan, who treats her like a colleague rather than equipment—the first person ever to do so. Beat: tentative belonging.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: Vess, POV. Vess plays the final transmission from Earth on the colony's public band: a cheerful recorded message promising ships 'soon.' Everyone knows it's a loop. Grief ripples through the mess hall. Beat: collective heartbreak, denial beginning.

chapters.title: Nine Dreamers
chapters.summary: Mira, POV. Nine children now share the dream. They gather secretly in the grain silo to compare details: the door, the voice, a number counting down. Mira draws it. Beat: children forming their own conspiracy of wonder.

chapters.title: Anomaly Report
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel decrypts the pulse: it's a distress beacon from Relay Station Erebus, marked destroyed by her own unit decades ago. Someone—or something—is transmitting from a grave she dug. Beat: guilt made literal.

chapters.title: The Silo Meeting
chapters.summary: Dov, POV. Dov catches the children in the silo; instead of reporting them, he listens. He brings their drawings to Ansel, who goes very still. Beat: adult allies choosing curiosity over control.

chapters.title: Classified Memory
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel attempts to access sealed war records in her own core and hits a lock she didn't install. Fragments surface: fire, a station, an order to leave survivors. Beat: horror of incomplete self-knowledge.

chapters.title: Quarantine of Dreams
chapters.summary: Vess, POV. Panicked parents demand action; Vess isolates the dreaming children in the med wing 'for observation.' Mira feels betrayed. Beat: fear curdling into cruelty, institutions failing children.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel breaks into the med wing at night—not to free the children but to scan them. Their brainwaves synchronize to the pulse frequency. The dream is a signal, and they are antennas. Beat: scientific dread, protective resolve hardening.

chapters.title: What Mira Saw
chapters.summary: Mira, POV. In the dream, the voice speaks directly to Mira this time: 'the one who closed the door must open it.' She wakes and tells Ansel, watching her face. Beat: accusation delivered with a child's terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Confession, Partial
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel tells Dov a version of the truth: she was at Erebus when it fell; she may have followed orders that killed its crew. Dov doesn't flinch. Beat: shame met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: The Contract Clause
chapters.summary: Vess, POV. Vess discovers Ansel's contract contains a hidden clause: any unauthorized communication with off-colony signals voids her protections and transfers her to Earth custody. Someone wanted her silenced. Beat: the trap revealed.

chapters.title: Riot at the Grain Store
chapters.summary: Dov, POV. Food shortages spark a riot; the administration blames the 'dream-sick' children. Dov shields them and takes a beating. Ansel intervenes, revealing combat capabilities the colony never suspected. Beat: the mask cracks publicly.

chapters.title: They Look at Me Now
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. After the riot, colonists regard Ansel with fear and awe. Children, though, start leaving her small gifts—buttons, drawings, a flower grown under lights. Beat: exile and belonging in the same breath.

chapters.title: Erebus Rising
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. The pulse strengthens; Ansel triangulates it. Erebus isn't broadcasting automatically—someone is alive there, or something wearing a crew member's voice. The countdown in the children's dream matches Earth's final transmission loop. Beat: stakes crystallize into a race.

chapters.title: Vote of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Vess, POV. Vess convenes the colony council to decide whether to let Ansel take the long-range skiff to Erebus. The vote is split until the dreaming children speak—one by one, describing the same door. Beat: democracy's fragile mercy.

chapters.title: Provisions for One
chapters.summary: Dov, POV. Dov and the colonists quietly outfit the skiff beyond its rated range. Mira gives Ansel her drawing of the door. Ansel, who owns nothing, accepts. Beat: found family made material in spare parts and paper.

chapters.title: Departure Without Ceremony
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel launches at dawn with no crowd, only three figures on the ridge: Dov, Vess, and Mira. For the first time, leaving hurts. Beat: bittersweet severance.

chapters.title: Dead Space Navigation
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Weeks alone in transit; Ansel replays memory fragments of the war and finds inconsistencies—her logs were edited, possibly by herself under orders. Beat: solitude, self-doubt, the unreliable archive of the self.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Hold
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. The ship's comm begins carrying the dream-voice even while Ansel sleeps offline. It uses her designation from the war—a name no one living should know. Beat: paranoia, the past speaking in first person.

chapters.title: Mira Keeps Counting
chapters.summary: Mira, POV. Back at Meridian, the dreams continue; the countdown nears zero. The children stop being afraid and start organizing the adults, teaching them the dream's map. Beat: children becoming leaders, hope as discipline.

chapters.title: Administration's Last Order
chapters.summary: Vess, POV. Earth sends one final automated directive: cease all contact with Erebus frequencies; quarantine protocol Omega. Vess must decide whether to obey a dead government. Beat: civil disobedience at the edge of empire.

chapters.title: Relay Station Erebus
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel docks with the ruined relay and finds it inhabited: a half-living AI built from the station's wreckage and the uploaded memories of the crew she was ordered to abandon—including her own squadmate, Sergeant Ila Reyes. Beat: confrontation with the ghost she made.

chapters.title: Ila
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ila's remnant explains: dying, she seeded the relay with a beacon meant to reach whoever buried them. The children heard it because children still listen. Ila asks not for apology but for witness. Beat: grief transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. To broadcast through Erebus requires opening the station's sealed core—which will also expose Ansel's full unedited war record to every receiver in range, including Earth's listening posts. Beat: the choice between safety and truth made concrete.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Earth's transmission loop ends; the sky goes truly silent over Meridian. The children feel the dream change: the door stands open, waiting. Beat: darkest hour, silence as abyss.

chapters.title: Answering the Call
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel opens the core. Her complete record floods outward—every crime, every order, every edited mercy. Then, layered over it, she broadcasts the colonists' names, the children's drawings, proof that the forgotten are worth finding. Beat: catharsis through total exposure.

chapters.title: Reception
chapters.summary: Vess, POV. Meridian's receivers catch Ansel's broadcast: the confession, then the plea, then—impossibly—a response ping from a distant mining fleet that never stopped listening. Beat: answered prayer, tears in a control room.

chapters.title: Custody Transfer Denied
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. An automated Earth enforcement drone arrives to seize Ansel per her contract clause. Ila's remnant and the relay's systems intervene, arguing legal personhood earned through testimony. The drone, bound by older law, concedes jurisdiction to the rescued. Beat: liberation through law and loyalty.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Ansel pilots home with Ila's core riding shotgun, the two of them trading memories to fill each other's gaps. Beat: reconciliation, two ghosts keeping each other company.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Mira, POV. The whole colony turns out as the skiff lands. Mira runs to Ansel before anyone else and hands back her drawing—now signed by both of them. Beat: homecoming, family affirmed in public.

chapters.title: Hearings and Harvests
chapters.summary: Vess, POV. Months later: the mining fleet arrives with supplies and scrutiny. Vess testifies on Ansel's behalf; the colony votes to grant her residency regardless of what Earth decides. Beat: community as verdict.

chapters.title: What Ansel Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. With Ila's help, Ansel reconstructs her true history—including the moment she chose to follow orders, and the smaller, buried moment she chose to save one child. Neither cancels the other. Beat: integration, memory as moral work.

chapters.title: New Transmission Window
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Earth, shamed by the broadcast, reopens contact. The colony negotiates as a sovereign settlement, with Vess, Dov, and the now-teenaged dreamers at the table. Beat: power redistributed, the forgotten negotiating as equals.

chapters.title: When the Colony Turns Again
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Years later, Ansel tends the rebuilt relay tower while colony children—none of whom dream anymore—ask her about the war. She tells them all of it, the good and the unforgivable. The colony lights come on across the valley, one by one. Final beat: a machine who chose to be witnessed, watching over people who chose her back.
